note: The workflow changes approved for the historical-data handoff. Read by guard_update_yml.py (Python guards) and tests/approved_workflows.js (JavaScript guards). update.yml must differ from the commit by EXACTLY these added lines (an empty difference is fine once they are committed); the two historical workflows must be byte-for-byte the pinned versions. Any other edit to these files, or any edit to another workflow, still trips the protected-file guards. Changing them again means updating this file on purpose. It also records the one approved change to each of fundamentals_updater.py and financials_updater.py (the five-stock test batch, research_test_batch.py): each file must differ from the commit by EXACTLY the listed diff lines (an empty difference is fine once they are committed). Stage 4 (SENSEX publication guard): update.yml and market_data.yml each differ from the commit by EXACTLY the four lines of the SENSEX guard (the closed approval variable on the Build site folder step and the sensex_publish.py call after the last copy); the earlier historical-handoff lines of update.yml are already committed. Stage 6B: .github/workflows/sensex_data.yml (the manual, non-publishing SENSEX pipeline) is a NEW file pinned byte for byte by SHA-256, like the two historical workflows; any edit to it needs this record updated on purpose. Stage 9D (market activity in the daily build): update.yml differs from the commit by EXACTLY the added lines listed under update_yml: one continue-on-error step that runs market_data_updater.py then validate_market_outputs.py and, if either fails, removes the four derived market_*.json files and exits non-zero; and, before the SENSEX guard, rm -f of _site/out/index_history.json, market_breadth.json, market_movers.json and market_dma.json (only market_activity.json stays eligible). Once committed, the difference is empty again. Stage NIFTY-refresh: historical.yml gained a weekday 19:00 IST schedule (13:30 UTC) and its hand-over, upload and save steps now also run for scheduled runs (never for a push), so the NIFTY 50 benchmark in historical/historical.json is refreshed after every trading session; its pin was updated on purpose. NIFTY 50 freshness warning: historical_updater.py differs from the commit by EXACTLY the listed lines (expected_latest_day, freshness_warning and their use in main(), a warning only; no retry, no change to errors, merge or validation); an empty difference is fine once they are committed. Stale-history fix: Upstox serves a day's daily candle only from about 07:00 IST the next day, so historical.yml now runs Tuesday to Saturday at 08:00 IST (02:30 UTC) and also refreshes every stock that already has saved history (HISTORICAL_REFRESH_SAVED on scheduled runs only); update.yml gained one second schedule line (Tuesday to Saturday 10:00 IST) that publishes it, listed under update_yml; historical_updater.py differs from the commit by EXACTLY the listed lines (published_through, weekdays_behind, saved_symbols, the stale headline and error annotation); the pin of historical.yml was updated on purpose. An empty difference is fine once they are committed. Universe-wide coverage fixes (Oct 2026 review, base 4eb39f7): update.yml differs by EXACTLY the added lines now listed (step ids, the run-status directory, the quarterly_calls input read through QUARTERLY_MAX_CALLS_OVERRIDE, the Report-the-data-steps step and the data-status job; the earlier added lines are committed); historical.yml is re-pinned (its cache is saved under side-historical-*, which the publishing run never restores). coverage_fixes_changes records the exact diff of each file this change touches (four updaters, and the one cache-key line of market_data.yml and financial_history.yml); for those paths it is the approved state, and updater_changes keeps the earlier, already committed records unchanged. Fundamentals for the whole universe in batches: fundamentals_updater.py differs by exactly the lines listed under coverage_fixes_changes (batch plan, gate, checkpoint and resume, back-off, invalid-record detection, the coverage report and the offline report/validate commands); .github/workflows/fundamentals_batch.yml is a NEW manual workflow pinned byte for byte by SHA-256, like sensex_data.yml.

added_lines: actions: read                         # only to list the saved caches when no fundamentals state was restored (cache-miss recovery below)
# Cache-miss recovery for fundamentals. Without its saved state the fundamentals step would start from nothing and publish only the few stocks one
# run can fetch. The combined actions/cache step above only has a `cache-hit` output (an empty string for "nothing restored" and "false" for a
# prefix match look alike), so the cache it resolved to is read with a second, read-only lookup (actions/cache/restore, lookup-only: it downloads
# nothing and writes nothing; its `cache-matched-key` is the documented output). With no state in the workspace the run is exactly one of:
#   lookup unavailable        -> stop (a missing cache cannot be told apart from a failed restore);
#   a cache was resolved      -> stop: it was not restored, or it holds no fundamentals state (another workflow's cache can be the newest one);
#   no cache resolved, but the complete cache list (every cache of this ref AND the default branch, which is what a restore can read, filtered for the
#     prefix nse-data- here) shows caches, or cannot be
#   no cache resolved and the complete list is empty (a genuine miss) -> recover from the published site, validated before anything is written.
# Every stop leaves the site exactly as it is (the deploy job needs this job) and names the condition and a safe remedy. Nothing here deletes a cache.
- name: Look up which saved cache the restore resolved to (no download)
- name: Check the restored fundamentals state

stop() { echo "::error::$1"; shift; for l in "$@"; do echo "$l"; done; echo "Nothing was published and nothing was changed."; exit 1; }
